message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | List required specs: CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling. |
| 2 | **Gather Parts** | All components must be compatible. | Use a PC build calculator (e.g., PCPartPicker) to avoid conflicts. |
| 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area. | Anti‑static wrist strap or mat; avoid carpet. |
| 4 | **Open the Case** | Access internal bays. | Remove side panel(s); keep screws handy. |
| 5 | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all components. | Place PSU with fan facing down or out; secure with screws. |
| 6 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Base for all other parts. | Align standoffs, screw in, then attach I/O shield. |
| 7 | **Install the CPU** | Central processing unit. | Open socket latch, align CPU (triangle marker), gently place, lock latch. |
| 8 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Prevent overheating. | Use a pea‑size amount; spread evenly. Attach cooler per instructions. |
| 9 | **Insert RAM Modules** | Memory for multitasking. | Open slots, align notch, press until clicks. |
|10 | **Mount Storage Drives** | SSD/HDD for OS & data. | 2.5″ SSDs go in M.2 or 2.5″ bays; 3.5″ HDDs in 3.5″ bays. |
|11 | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Visual output & gaming. | Insert into top PCI‑e slot, secure with screws, connect power cables. |
|12 | **Connect Power Cables** | Power all components. | PSU 24‑pin to motherboard, 8‑pin CPU, GPU power, storage, fans. |
|13 | **Connect Data Cables** | Data transfer. | SATA cables to drives, M.2 connectors, front panel headers (USB, audio, power button). |
|14 | **Cable Management** | Improves airflow & aesthetics. | Tuck cables behind motherboard tray, use zip ties. |
|15 | **Close the Case** | Protect components. | Reattach side panel, secure screws. |
|16 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Verify hardware, set boot order. | Press power button, enter BIOS (usually DEL/F2). Check CPU, RAM, storage detection. |
|17 | **Install Operating System (OS)** | Turn your PC into a working machine. | USB flash drive with Windows 10/11 or Linux installer. Follow on‑screen prompts. |
|18 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure hardware works optimally. | Download latest drivers from manufacturer sites. Run Windows Update or Linux updates. |
|19 | **Test & Benchmark** | Confirm stability. | Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, Cinebench). Monitor temperatures. |
|20 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep system running smoothly. | Clean dust every 3–6 months, update drivers, monitor temperatures. |

---

#### Quick Checklist

- **CPU** – Intel i5/i7/i9 or AMD Ryzen 5/7/9
- **Motherboard** – Matching socket, chipset, form factor (ATX, mATX, ITX)
- **RAM** – 16 GB DDR4/DDR5 (minimum 8 GB for basic use)
- **Storage** – NVMe SSD (250 GB+) + optional HDD (1 TB+)
- **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX 3060/3070 or AMD RX 6600/6700 (or integrated if not gaming)
- **PSU** – 550 W–750 W 80+ Gold (adjust for GPU power)
- **Case** – ATX mid‑tower with good airflow
- **Cooling** – Stock cooler or aftermarket air/liquid cooler
- **Peripherals** – Monitor, keyboard, mouse, speakers/headset

---

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Short‑circuit** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; double‑check standoffs. |
| **Overheating** | Ensure proper thermal paste, adequate case airflow, fan curves. |
| **Component incompatibility** | Verify socket, chipset, BIOS version before buying. |
| **Insufficient PSU** | Calculate total wattage; add 20–30 % headroom. |
| **Loose screws** | Tighten all screws, especially motherboard standoffs and PSU. |
| **Boot failure** | Check all connections, especially CPU cooler, RAM, GPU. |

---

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build planner & price comparison.  
- **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware.  
- **Forums** – r/buildapc (Reddit), Tom’s Hardware, AnandTech.  
- **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, GPU manuals.

---

### Final Thought

Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you full control over performance and future upgrades. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for help—happy building!
